Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

The strongest solo Paladin build available this season, which is a smaller claim than it sounds and the summary says so on purpose. The damage is Physical Thorns rather than weapon hits: 'this build is using Shield Charge to deal Physical Thorns damage to your enemies through direct hits and Retribution pulsing around you everytime you block'. Shield Charge is the engine because its short-channel variant carries the Hit Count As Blocking modifier, so driving through a pack counts as blocks and pulses Retribution - which makes positioning the actual skill of the build, 'maximize the amount of enemies you hit with it by positioning accordingly'. Around it, Clash must be recast at least once every six seconds for Retribution chance, Thorns and Block Chance; Condemn gathers and applies Vulnerable, Weaken and Unhindered; Fortress is a three-second immunity that also converts Resolve into a large damage burst; and the two auras supply crit chance, Fortify, Resolve generation and Unstoppable. Everything scales through Resolve, capped at exactly 30 by three greater +6 Maximum Resolve tempers plus Aspect of Glynn's Anvil and the Phoba of Righteous Will charm set. Standing, honestly: Maxroll's overall endgame list rates this A and it is the best-rated Paladin build there, with five Paladin builds in C and two in D behind it; Maxroll's push list also rates it A. TierListHQ rates the class B, recording that the 3.1.0 launch buffs 'didn't translate to Pit performance', and the only S-tier Paladin entry anywhere is an explicitly group-only support build. Icy Veins dissents hard with two S-tier Paladin builds, but its list is dated 2026-07-04, before 3.1.1 and 3.1.2, and it is the season's known outlier. The guide's own cons are the right expectation-setter: short range, and requires good positioning - a melee thorns build has to physically drive through packs, which is exactly what a Pit boss floor punishes.

Rotation
  1. Condemn to gather the pack, Clash refreshed at least every six seconds, then Shield Charge repeatedly through the middle of the group so the hits count as blocks and pulse Retribution.
  2. Both auras up, and Fortress held as a planned cooldown for dangerous floors and bosses.
Variants

Leveling — Open with Condemn to pull the pack together, keep Clash refreshed, then Shield Charge repeatedly through the middle of the group so the blocks pulse Retribution. Drop Fortress when you are surrounded or on a boss for the immunity and damage window, and use Defiance Aura's active to break crowd control.
Move on when Mantle of the Grey in the chest and Herald of Zakarum in the shield slot - the guide's own difference between Starter and Midgame - with Tibault's Will following.

Early Endgame — Identical to the previous stage: Condemn to gather, Clash at least every six seconds, Shield Charge as the spam through the middle of the pack, Fortress for immunity and its Resolve damage bonus.
Move on when The three uniques equipped and the Resolve tempering chase underway - at which point the build stops being about acquisition and starts being about hitting two hard caps.

Late Endgame — Unchanged from the early endgame. This stage is a tempering and masterworking project, not a gameplay change - which is worth saying plainly, because a build page that implies a new rotation at every stage is lying about what the guide actually publishes.
Move on when Resolve at 30 with Block and Critical Strike Chance capped on masterworked gear. Then swap to the push variant's Mythic and charm-set layout.

Pushing — The same loop, played more carefully. Fortress becomes a planned cooldown for dangerous floors rather than a free button, and you pre-gather with Condemn before every Shield Charge pass - because the guide's two cons, short range and required positioning, bite hardest exactly here.

Stat requirements
  • Reach the Resolve cap of 30
Records
  • Pit 125 clear + Tormented Mephisto (creator's own video claim, not a leaderboard placement; no season or date stated) Proof →
Lootfilter

Shield Charge Paladin — Maxroll Light / Medium / Strict (in-guide import codes) — View Filter

maxroll.gg

The guide ships three strictness tiers as import codes in its Loot Filter section; those are the exact match and its own caveat is that 'these provide a baseline you can adjust to your own liking'. The community sites were checked: the Paladin filters surfaced on diablo4lootfilter.com appear to be Season 13 and none is Shield-Charge-specific, so none is linked here rather than a stale mismatch being presented as an alternative.

Uniques
  • chest Target-farm Harbinger of Hatred. Crafting priority #1 in every variant - it is one of the three things Resolve scales your damage through, alongside the Juggernaut Oath and the Sentinel glyph. Where →
  • offhand Target-farm Astaroth. The build's shield, and last on the Mythic crafting order because the other three do more for you first. Where →
  • pants No dedicated boss - it sits in the General Unique Pool, so any boss can drop it and the reliable route is the Horadric Cube: Common pants plus Primordial Dust rerolls into a random pants-slot unique. Crafting priority #2. Where →
  • amulet Push variant only, where it slots in at crafting priority #2 ahead of Tibault's Will. General Unique Pool - any boss encounter - or the Horadric Cube. Remember the standing rule the guide restates: you can equip only one Mythic crafted in the Horadric Cube, but any number acquired elsewhere. Where →

Point allocation, in order83 points across 24 nodes

Recorded from the guide's own Maxroll planner profile, not from the guide page -- the page renders its tree from the planner and carries no node text at all. Points are the profile's own allocation; skills rank to 15 and most upgrade mods to 3. This stage records the guide's Starter profile.

Skill point priority

  1. Scope note: this is an endgame-only guide - it 'assumes you have a Level 70 Character and unlocked Torment 1' and links three separate Paladin levelling guides - so this stage records its Starter variant rather than a 1-70 route it never published
  2. Shield Charge is the main damage: always position to hit the most enemies so Hit Count As Blocking triggers as often as possible
  3. Clash keeps its buff up - one cast per six seconds minimum - and is your Retribution chance, Thorns and Block Chance
  4. Fanaticism Aura ranks: 14% critical strike chance at 15 ranks, and the source of Vulnerable, Weaken and Fortify
  5. Defiance Aura ranks for health recovery and Resolve generation, and it can be activated for Unstoppable
  6. Fortress for the three-second immunity plus its Resolve damage bonus; Condemn for grouping and Unhindered

Skill point priority

  1. Reach the Resolve cap of 30, and know the arithmetic: 'your basline maximum Resolve is 8 and you need 3x +6 Maximum Resolve Tempers, Aspect of Glynn's Anvil and the Phoba of Righteous Will set to reach exactly 30 Maximum Resolve'. The temper needs to crit and then Masterwork-crit to reach +6
  2. Cap Block Chance through Aegis at rank 15, the Castle and Shield Bearer boards, Aspect of Interdiction and Bulwark's Aspect
  3. Cap Critical Strike Chance through Fanaticism Aura ranks, charm and seal affixes, weapon tempers and Masterwork focus
  4. Then, and only then, chase Critical Strike Damage: 'the value of Critical Strike Damage multiplier goes up as you can acquire more Critical Strike Chance. If you have very low Critical Strike Chance, Physical Damage, Vulnerable Damage or All Damage multipliers have more value'
  5. Defensively, 'focus on Armor and Maximum Life and the Aspects provided in the planner'

How to run them

Identical across all four variants: hire Raheir, who 'grants you Bastion and Inspiration to buff your damage', and reinforce with Aldkin, who 'reduces enemy damage and slows with Field of Languish'. Note this is the opposite emphasis from most Season 14 builds, which take Raheir purely for survivability - here Inspiration is picked up as a damage node, which is the tell that this build already has its own defence covered by block, Resolve and Fortress and is spending the mercenary slot on offence and on the damage-reduction layer instead.

Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

The strongest solo Paladin build available this season, which is a smaller claim than it sounds and the summary says so on purpose. The damage is Physical Thorns rather than weapon hits: 'this build is using Shield Charge to deal Physical Thorns damage to your enemies through direct hits and Retribution pulsing around you everytime you block'. Shield Charge is the engine because its short-channel variant carries the Hit Count As Blocking modifier, so driving through a pack counts as blocks and pulses Retribution - which makes positioning the actual skill of the build, 'maximize the amount of enemies you hit with it by positioning accordingly'. Around it, Clash must be recast at least once every six seconds for Retribution chance, Thorns and Block Chance; Condemn gathers and applies Vulnerable, Weaken and Unhindered; Fortress is a three-second immunity that also converts Resolve into a large damage burst; and the two auras supply crit chance, Fortify, Resolve generation and Unstoppable. Everything scales through Resolve, capped at exactly 30 by three greater +6 Maximum Resolve tempers plus Aspect of Glynn's Anvil and the Phoba of Righteous Will charm set. Standing, honestly: Maxroll's overall endgame list rates this A and it is the best-rated Paladin build there, with five Paladin builds in C and two in D behind it; Maxroll's push list also rates it A. TierListHQ rates the class B, recording that the 3.1.0 launch buffs 'didn't translate to Pit performance', and the only S-tier Paladin entry anywhere is an explicitly group-only support build. Icy Veins dissents hard with two S-tier Paladin builds, but its list is dated 2026-07-04, before 3.1.1 and 3.1.2, and it is the season's known outlier. The guide's own cons are the right expectation-setter: short range, and requires good positioning - a melee thorns build has to physically drive through packs, which is exactly what a Pit boss floor punishes.

Rotation
  1. Condemn to gather the pack, Clash refreshed at least every six seconds, then Shield Charge repeatedly through the middle of the group so the hits count as blocks and pulse Retribution.
  2. Both auras up, and Fortress held as a planned cooldown for dangerous floors and bosses.
Variants

Leveling — Open with Condemn to pull the pack together, keep Clash refreshed, then Shield Charge repeatedly through the middle of the group so the blocks pulse Retribution. Drop Fortress when you are surrounded or on a boss for the immunity and damage window, and use Defiance Aura's active to break crowd control.
Move on when Mantle of the Grey in the chest and Herald of Zakarum in the shield slot - the guide's own difference between Starter and Midgame - with Tibault's Will following.

Early Endgame — Identical to the previous stage: Condemn to gather, Clash at least every six seconds, Shield Charge as the spam through the middle of the pack, Fortress for immunity and its Resolve damage bonus.
Move on when The three uniques equipped and the Resolve tempering chase underway - at which point the build stops being about acquisition and starts being about hitting two hard caps.

Late Endgame — Unchanged from the early endgame. This stage is a tempering and masterworking project, not a gameplay change - which is worth saying plainly, because a build page that implies a new rotation at every stage is lying about what the guide actually publishes.
Move on when Resolve at 30 with Block and Critical Strike Chance capped on masterworked gear. Then swap to the push variant's Mythic and charm-set layout.

Pushing — The same loop, played more carefully. Fortress becomes a planned cooldown for dangerous floors rather than a free button, and you pre-gather with Condemn before every Shield Charge pass - because the guide's two cons, short range and required positioning, bite hardest exactly here.

Uniques
  • chest Target-farm Harbinger of Hatred. Crafting priority #1 in every variant - it is one of the three things Resolve scales your damage through, alongside the Juggernaut Oath and the Sentinel glyph. Where →
  • offhand Target-farm Astaroth. The build's shield, and last on the Mythic crafting order because the other three do more for you first. Where →
  • pants No dedicated boss - it sits in the General Unique Pool, so any boss can drop it and the reliable route is the Horadric Cube: Common pants plus Primordial Dust rerolls into a random pants-slot unique. Crafting priority #2. Where →
  • amulet Push variant only, where it slots in at crafting priority #2 ahead of Tibault's Will. General Unique Pool - any boss encounter - or the Horadric Cube. Remember the standing rule the guide restates: you can equip only one Mythic crafted in the Horadric Cube, but any number acquired elsewhere. Where →
